A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaVAction research, and their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. V2 substantially expands and reorganizes the work.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, training experiments, ablations and qualitative analyses on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 and additional video benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds cross-domain evaluations, attention analyses, difficulty-stratified results and further ablations.

M1.justification: The documented core procedure retains hard-distractor training, the supervised action token, temporal detection, direct prediction and prior-action conditioning. V2's named two-stage pipeline elaborates the specialist top-K refinement already described in v1 Sections 3.1.1 and 5.2 and used in Table 4. The additional backbone and dataset applications do not establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds EPFL-Smart-Kitchen-30, MECCANO and Animal Kingdom, extending evaluation to another cooking population, assembly activities and simultaneous animal actions. Additional MLLM evaluation expands from six to thirteen benchmarks, adding captioning and open-ended tasks through VDC, VideoDC, VideoEval-Pro, ActNet-QA, VideoChatGPT, CVRR and TempCompass.

E2.justification: V2 adds IPL to the existing EPIC comparison and evaluates VideoMAE, multi-modal VideoMAE, SlowFast and InternVL3-8B variants in the new domain experiments. Appendix E.3 also introduces multi-round appending as a structured-output comparator. The comparator roster in the general video benchmark table otherwise remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot second-stage and finetuned EPFL evaluations with shared top-five candidate filtering, one-epoch MECCANO finetuning, and Animal Kingdom evaluation using Jaccard accuracy and an InternVL3-8B configuration. V2 also introduces attention aggregation, GPT-4o difficulty grading and experiments varying K during both training and testing. These are additional evaluation designs, rather than demonstrated reruns of all retained experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds attention analysis and visualization, difficulty-stratified accuracy, AVION–TIM distribution comparisons and K sensitivity, action-token number and supervision-layer ablations, and structured-output accuracy and computational-cost comparisons. These test mechanisms and design choices beyond v1's additive and leave-one-out ablations. Existing benchmark subcategory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports JSD as 0.674 ± 0.089, a 95% confidence interval, p < 0.001 and Cohen's d = 7.57 over 9,668 validation samples. This adds statistical reporting for one supporting analysis; the estimation and testing procedures are insufficiently specified. Neither version reports repeated-training-run or seed uncertainty for the principal accuracy results.

E6.justification: New results include EPFL accuracies of 36.2 zero-shot and 46.6 finetuned, MECCANO accuracy of 51.7, Animal Kingdom Jaccard scores of 61.0 and 58.7, and seven additional MLLM benchmark columns. Leave-one-out results change, including full-model 73.4 to 74.1 and without-AVION 68.2 to 69.7, without establishing identical settings. The 16-frame EPIC classification rows disappear; the 32-frame scores and original six additional benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The distractor-sampling formulation, temporal-padding equations, action-token hidden-state notation and prior-action objective are mathematically retained, sometimes consolidated or moved inline. Neither version contains theoretical proofs, and v2's new attention and distribution analyses are empirical rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the central contribution from action recognition centered on EPIC-KITCHENS to fine-grained action understanding across domains and output formats. The introduction claims SOTA on four action-recognition datasets and improvements on ten MLLM benchmarks, versus v1's EPIC-focused SOTA and five additional benchmark improvements. Structured-action prediction is also promoted to a principal contribution.

C2.justification: V2 introduces interpretations linking stronger visual attention and action-token aggregation to improved recognition, argues robustness across semantic difficulty levels, and uses distribution and K analyses to support the OOD interpretation. It explicitly discusses the structured pipeline's first-stage recall ceiling and restriction to applications requiring structured actions. Earlier narration-bias and unsuccessful chain-of-thought discussions remain, largely in the appendices.

D1.justification: V2 adds the difficulty-assessment prompt, attention-computation instructions, KV-cache details for multi-round appending, and inference costs of approximately 820 versus 4.3 GPU hours. Its availability statement now includes data and the benchmark alongside code and models. Core training hardware, learning rates, epochs and existing task prompts are retained, while some earlier dataset and benchmark descriptions are removed.

R1.justification: The research positioning is substantially revised. V2 explicitly distinguishes fine-grained action contrastiveness from InsTALL's procedural assistance, HAIC's captioning and MotionLLM's motion understanding, and adds literature supporting new benchmarks, structured-action applications and attention analysis. V1's standalone vision-centric MLLM survey and several broader literature discussions are removed or condensed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 separates data reformulation from model design, combines experimental setup and results, redistributes discussion into appendices, and adds distinct conclusion and ethics sections. Terminology also changes, including official keys to action labels and prior-action memory to temporal order learning.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, redraws the pipeline diagram and rearranges Figure 1. It adds an attention visualization and several experimental tables, and substantially expands and groups the general benchmark table by output format. Earlier qualitative figures and the verb/noun performance plot are retained with resizing, relabeling and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of generalization and design choices through independent cooking, assembly and animal evaluations, broader output-format testing, and token-design and structured-output ablations. These address important coverage and diagnostic gaps in v1 while retaining its principal results. Some new support remains weak: Appendix D changes training and testing K together when interpreting overfitting, statistical procedures are underspecified, and revised ablation settings are unclear. Nevertheless, the additional controlled comparisons and cross-domain evidence provide a substantial net quality improvement.
